questions.answer: Chaotic, you cannot count on the course catalogue to be up to date

questions.answer: Trial and error, then asking other exchange students if they have the same problem

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not really, there are the course catalogue, module handbook and the course sign up. In the module handbook you will find courses or modules that may or may not still be available, and information about language ECTS and so forth may not be either updated, or available about the course. Then the course catalogue, you will find that the course you thought were in the module handbook are in fact not available, or not in English as you thought, or has a different ECTS credit than previously read, or the course might not exist anymore. Then there is the course sign up, each professor decides when the course sign up opens and ends, instead of one collected sign up period, courses that you thought you could take you probably cannot take, and then if you sign up for a course, you might not be guaranteed a spot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buckle up, it's chaos and shenanigans, and honestly a bit unprofessional, my advice: sign up for whatever you can find in English, sign up for more than 30 in case you would need a backup, and you'll need it
